q-33451.name: Question 1
q-33451.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(2,0,-5)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $(r-[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}])\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=0.$
q-33451.worked_solution:
Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(6,3,1).$ Then 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3 \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector $n=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|4\cdot 1+3\cdot 2+6\cdot 3|}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|4+6+18|}{\sqrt{1+4+9}} \\  & =\frac{|28|}{\sqrt{14}} \\  & =2\sqrt{14}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨6,-1,4⟩-⟨-4,3,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨10,-4,5⟩.\end{aligned}

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|10\cdot 4+(-4)\cdot 0+5\cdot (-3)|}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-3)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|40+0-15|}{\sqrt{16+9}} \\  & =\frac{|25|}{\sqrt{25}} \\  & =\frac{25}{5} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}

Finally, the shortest distance from the point P to the plane Π is the absolute value of the scalar projection of PQ→ onto the normal vector of the plane:

d=|compnPQ→|=|PQ→⋅n||n|=|(−7)⋅(−2)+(−3)⋅(−3)+(−5)⋅6|(−2)2+(−3)2+(6)2=|14+9−30|4+9+36=|−7|49=77=1.
